stem: A verbal adult has a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15, with all three components testable. Which interpretation is accurate?

options.A: This is the highest possible GCS total when all three components are testable, reflecting the best eye, verbal, and motor responses.
options.B: This is the lowest possible total GCS score, reflecting absent eye, verbal, and motor responses.
options.C: This score is outside the valid GCS range because the scale permits only total scores from 3 through 14.
options.D: This score by itself indicates severe traumatic brain injury and independently requires endotracheal intubation.

rationale: The official Glasgow Coma Scale resource states that the composite score ranges from 3 to 15, with 3 the lowest possible score and 15 the highest. With all three components testable, 15 represents the maximum total. B and C misstate the scoring range, and D incorrectly interprets a maximum score as severe traumatic brain injury or a standalone airway indication.
educational_objective: Interpret a fully testable GCS total of 15 as the maximum possible composite score, while remembering that component responses should also be documented.
source_organization: Glasgow Coma Scale official educational resource, University of Glasgow team

source_claim_supported: The composite GCS score is the sum of eye, verbal, and motor response scores; its possible range is 3–15, with 15 the highest possible total.

source_original.stem: A verbal adult has a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 15, with all three components testable. Which interpretation is accurate?

options.A: This is the highest possible GCS total, reflecting maximum eye, verbal, and motor responses in all three testable domains overall.
options.B: This is the lowest possible total GCS score, reflecting absent eye, verbal, and motor responses at the time of the neurologic assessment.
options.C: This score is outside the valid GCS range and should be discarded because the scale permits only total scores from 3 through 14.
options.D: This score by itself indicates severe traumatic brain injury and is an independent indication for immediate endotracheal intubation.

source_original.rationale: The Glasgow Coma Scale total ranges from 3 to 15, and 15 is the highest possible total when all components are testable. Option A is correct. Option B incorrectly calls 15 the lowest score. Option C falsely treats a valid score as outside the scale. Option D incorrectly interprets a normal maximum score as severe traumatic brain injury and an independent indication for intubation.
source_original.source_detail: Official Glasgow Coma Scale — What is GCS?/Derived indices and FAQ: eye, verbal, and motor components can yield a composite total from 3 to 15 when all components are testable; 15 is the highest possible total. correction_summary: Retained key and range. Simplified the keyed wording and avoided calling GCS 15 universally 'normal consciousness' in the item, because total scores should be interpreted alongside component findings and clinical context.

audit_findings.claim_audit: 3–15 range and maximum 15 are direct source statements.

distractor_audit.D: 15 does not independently establish severe TBI or intubation need.

audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Preserved component-testable caveat and avoided overinterpreting the total score.
